intro: Armenia's political landscape is dominated by the release of a new draft constitution and Prime Minister Pashinyan's visit to Romania, while economic discussions focus on trade diversification and an AI education initiative.

topics.title: New Draft Constitution Sparks Political Debate
topics.text: Prime Minister Pashinyan has released a new draft constitution, prompting Ankara and Baku to hail the document while the domestic opposition coalition rejects it. Reports indicate the draft could allow courts to strip citizenship and removes a constitutional phrase that previously caused disputes with Turkey. Former President Robert Kocharyan, currently imprisoned, has reportedly not been given the opportunity to review the draft.

topics.title: Pashinyan Visits Romania to Strengthen Ties
topics.text: Prime Minister Pashinyan is on an official visit to Bucharest, where Armenia and Romania signed a strategic partnership declaration. Leaders from both countries emphasized the importance of developing trade and economic ties, with Romanian officials stating support for Armenia's EU integration and calling the visit a historic moment. An official welcoming ceremony was held ahead of the high-level meetings.

topics.title: Armenia-Russia Economic and Humanitarian Cooperation Discussed
topics.text: Armenian and Russian deputy prime ministers met in Moscow to discuss trade, economic, and humanitarian cooperation. Separately, the Armenian Deputy Prime Minister traveled to Moscow for a Eurasian Economic Commission Council meeting. Armenian infrastructure officials also held meetings in Ashgabat, Turkmenistan.

topics.title: Armenia Advances EU Integration and Visa Liberalization
topics.text: Foreign Minister Mirzoyan briefed EU ambassadors on Armenia's approaches to signing a peace agreement with Azerbaijan and underscored the TRIPP project. The Interior Minister expects the first phase of the EU visa liberalization assessment to be fully completed by mid-2027. Discussions on deepening interparliamentary cooperation with Greece were also held.

topics.title: Firebird and UATE to Launch AI Education Hub in Hrazdan
topics.text: Firebird and the Union of Advanced Technology Enterprises (UATE) announced plans to launch an AI Education Hub in Hrazdan. In other technology news, AraratBank signed an MoU to implement an AI-powered CRM system, and discussions were held with SpaceX regarding the development of Starlink internet services in Armenia.

topics.title: Armenia to Host Major Basketball Championships in 2027 and 2028
topics.text: Armenia has been selected to host two FIBA European basketball championships in 2027 and 2028. The national shooting team is also preparing to compete in the Polish Open Kaliber 2026. Ararat-Armenia football club has departed for a training camp in Austria.

topics.title: Iran Warns Armenia Over 'Trump Route' Corridor
topics.text: Another Iranian official has issued a warning to Yerevan regarding the so-called 'Trump Route' transport corridor. Meanwhile, Azerbaijan's leader stated that the 'Zangezur Corridor' will contribute to the revival of the Silk Road, highlighting ongoing regional tensions over connectivity projects.
